candidates.reference_text: I've finally set out on the voyage of life for myself, leaving the family ark behind in New Haven. What makes me sad is the thought that I've gone away for good, and that from now on I'll be at home only as a visitor. Mother said this departure felt worse to her than when I went to Europe. I couldn't quite agree: Europe had been entirely new and untried, while this move has only transplanted me from one scene of student life to another. Among students, I usually feel more or less at home.

candidates.reference_text: I've never really been the person curled up on a couch with my nose in a book. As far back as I remember, I wanted to be outside getting into something. Every summer, we spent a week at my grandparents' place. My sister and I always wanted to play outdoors and explore, while my cousins were perfectly content inside, reading one book after another. I don't think books are bad—that isn't my point. I've tried books people recommended, and I always begin them; I just never seem to finish.

candidates.reference_text: I'm a Christmas nerd. And a candlelight nerd too. I love the warmth and atmosphere that real flames bring into a room. So I suppose I've become a sensitive, candle-checking Christmas nerd.

candidates.reference_text: My paternal grandmother lived about three hours from our family, so I normally saw her only once or twice a year. But during two summers, after third and fourth grades, I spent a week at Grandma's house with a cousin my age. Our days found a rhythm: morning chores, a walk to the neighborhood park and its wading pool, lunch, then an hour's rest because my cousin was recovering from scarlet fever. I usually read through the hour. Sometimes we played Go Fish with Grandma.
